Aurora Innovation signed a nonbinding memorandum of understanding Monday under which Charger Logistics intends to buy up to 500 Aurora Driver-powered trucks, with deliveries over 2027 and 2028. The deal builds on a contract Charger signed in July to start driverless hauls between Dallas and Laredo, Texas.
Under a final agreement, Charger would own the trucks and pay Aurora for the driving through its Driver as a Service model. Carrier-owned fleets are central to Aurora’s plan to run more than 30,000 driverless trucks by 2030.
Aurora now expects to pass 200 driverless trucks by the end of February , with its production ramp about six weeks behind plan. It still expects more than 1,000 by the end of 2027 . In April, Hirschbach Motor Lines signed a nonbinding MOU to own 500 Aurora trucks under the same ownership model.
Charger’s president tied the larger order to its first months running autonomous trucks on the border lane.
“Since launching autonomous operations along the Laredo corridor, we’ve realized immediate operational benefits that point to a clear path to scaling,” said Andy Khera, president of Charger Logistics. “Aurora’s plans to open long-haul, high-volume routes position us to scale geographically while we integrate autonomy from our TMS to the road, building a resilient and autonomous ecosystem for our customers.”
How Driver as a Service changes ownership
Charger’s July agreement is a Transport as a Service deal, according to Aurora’s third-quarter shareholder letter. Under that model, Aurora owns and operates the trucks and charges about $2 per mile, including a fuel surcharge.
Under Driver as a Service, the carrier buys the truck and pays Aurora for the driving. That brings Aurora 85 cents or more per mile, on trucks Aurora expects to run about 250,000 miles a year.
The letter calls the Charger deal “a potential multi-year revenue stream in the hundreds of millions of dollars.” Neither company disclosed Charger’s per-mile rate.
Aurora made the case for carrier ownership in the release.
“Owning the physical asset is the logical choice for our customers: it makes today’s operations more efficient and enables carriers to grow their business, keeping them competitive,” said Zac Andreoni, vice president of business development at Aurora.
The Charger deal is not yet binding
The cautionary statement in Aurora’s release lists the risk that the Charger MOU may not lead to a final agreement and binding orders “on the anticipated timeframe or at all.” In September, Aurora pushed back its own target for breakeven gross margin on a run-rate basis to the first half of 2027, at about 500 trucks, from the end of 2026.
Werner Enterprises, another Aurora customer, was still negotiating economic terms in September. Daragh Mahon, Werner’s executive vice president and chief information officer, addressed the cost on a customer panel at Aurora’s Analyst and Investor Day in Dallas on Sept. 23.
“And I will be quite honest that we have a gap. We’ve got to figure this out,” Mahon said.
Aurora ranks No. 4 on FreightTech 25
The MOU landed the same day FreightWaves named Aurora No. 4 on the 2027 FreightTech 25 , revealed at the F3 Awards Dinner in Chattanooga, Tennessee. Aurora previously ranked No. 2 on the 2026 list .
Four autonomous trucking companies made this year’s list, up from three last year: Aurora, Kodiak AI at No. 12, Torc Robotics at No. 19, and Waabi at No. 20.
Charger’s fleet and routes
Charger Logistics, a privately held, asset-based carrier, operates across the U.S. and Mexico. Its U.S. unit, Charger Logistics USA, lists 481 power units and 542 drivers in its Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration registration , last updated in October 2025. The 500 Aurora trucks would exceed that count.
Charger plans to run the Aurora trucks on current and new high-volume routes near the border and across the country.
“With the launch of our second-generation hardware and trucks, Aurora is ready to support our customers’ ambitions to grow their networks and move more freight with driverless trucks,” Andreoni said.
Why it matters: The deal would move the cost of owning driverless trucks from Aurora to the carrier. If the deal completes and the MOU fulfilled, Charger would take on more trucks than its U.S. unit runs today.

Why Is Lamborghini Taking So Long To Unveil the New Temerario Spyder?
10 photos
Photo: Instagram | niwwrd / fully_leaded
Lamborghini’s new-age lineup may be vast in terms of models, as it has three of them currently on sale: the Urus, Temerario, and Revuelto. However, it is quite limited when it comes to the derivatives of these vehicles.
You see, the only Urus currently on sale is the Lamborghini Urus SE Performante . It’s a plug-in hybrid model with 801 hp (812 ps/597 kW) and 738 pound-feet (1,000 Nm) of torque combined from its electrified twin-turbo 4-liter V8 engine. It weighs nearly 2.5 tons (5,452 pounds), takes 3.3 seconds from 0-62 mph (0-100 kph), maxes out at 194 mph (312 kph), and can drive on electric power for 37 miles (60 km) on the WLTP cycle.
The Revuelto lineup also consisted of a single member until a couple of months ago, when the company unveiled the Revuelto SV . The SuperVeloce has 1,050 hp (1,065 ps/783 kW) on tap and 1,051 lb-ft (1,425 Nm) of torque in total, reaches 62 mph (100 kph) in 2.4 seconds, and does 216 mph (348 kph) flat-out. It features a plug-in hybrid 6.5-liter naturally aspirated V12, just like the regular Revuelto, which has 1,001 hp (1,015/747 kW) in total, is 0.1 seconds slower to 62 mph, and does 217 mph (350 kph) flat-out.
We recently found out that Lamborghini appears to be cooking another special Revuelto. A mysterious prototype spotted in the open earlier this week was fully wrapped in camouflage, and even from beneath the trippy vinyl stickers, it still looked a lot more aggressive than the Revuelto SV. Word on the street is that it could be the Lamborghini Revuelto SVJ , with an obvious emphasis on the word “could,” because nobody who is not directly involved in its development knows anything about it.
Photo: Instagram | niwwrd / fully_leaded As for the Lamborghini Temerario , which replaced the Huracan in the company’s lineup, and is now the Raging Bull’s new “baby” supercar, it is limited to a single member. It hit the assembly line in 2025, and as you already know, it features a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8, assisted by three electric motors. The model is a PHEV with 907 hp (920 ps/677 kW) and 530 pound-feet (730 Nm) of torque combined, 0-62 mph (0-100 kph) in 2.7 seconds, and a 213 mph (343 kph) top speed.
However, given that its predecessors, namely the Huracan and Gallardo, were offered in all kinds of different versions, we can safely assume that it is only a matter of time until Lamborghini expands the Temerario lineup. And in fact, we know what the second member will be, because we have seen it testing on a few occasions these past few months, and it is none other than the Temerario Spyder.
As its name clearly implies, it is an open-top model , with a retractable roof that does not feature the double-bubble design of its fixed-roof sibling. The rear window is also significantly smaller, and it looks like the engine vents have been restyled. The roof should operate at the push of a button, lowering into a special compartment behind the seats, and rumor has it that this operation will take in the region of 17 seconds, though you may want to take it with a pinch of salt for now, for obvious reasons.
On the inside, it will look identical to the Lamborghini Temerario Coupe, and this will include the same 12.3-inch digital gauge cluster, 8.4 inch infotainment system with its portrait-like screen, buttons, and so on. The trim and upholstery could be different, though you shouldn’t quote us on that. The powertrain will also be identical to the Temerario Coupe, though due to the extra weight, we expect the Temerario Spyder to be a hair slower.
Photo: Instagram | niwwrd / fully_leaded Different outlets still believe that the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder might come out of hiding officially before the end of 2026, whereas others are convinced that we will likely see it in an official environment in the first half of 2027. What does this mean? That we also have no idea when this model is due, though if we were to bet on it, we’d say that probably in 2027. After all, it’s not like it’s open-top supercar season in the northern hemisphere anymore, is it?
Lamborghini is certainly taking its time before pulling the wraps off the Temerario Spyder, as it wants to make sure that everything functions as it should before introducing it, and putting it into production at the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory in Italy. Therefore, we expect to see more prototypes in the coming days / weeks / months, and we hope we eventually learn more about its special features that differentiate it from its fixed-roof sibling.
Meanwhile, we will leave you in the company of the renderings above in the gallery, shared on Instagram by @niwwrd, who quotes @fully_leaded as the pixel master behind the CGI clip embedded at the bottom of the page. So, if you had to choose between the Temerario Coupe and Spyder , which one would you get and why? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Niwwrd (@niwwrd)

2026 SEMA Show • Mitsubishi Returns to Las Vegas With the Fresh 2028 Outlander Diamond Trail Edition
1-of-10 Apollo EVO, the $3.3M Caribbean Dragon, Takes Vegas by Storm With Aspirated 800-HP V12
15 photos
Photo: Apollo Automobil
How did the most artistic Greek god come to ride on the backs of dragons all the way into the New World is something only the Germans can fully understand – and explain. However, due to their not-so-vocal nature, the Germans prefer to do instead of say, so that’s how the Apollo EVO Caribbean Dragon flapped its naturally-aspirated V12 hypercar wings all the way to America.
Traditional European fire-breathing wyverns rarely appear in indigenous Caribbean folklore, where draconic legends instead manifest as primordial giant serpents and abyssal sea monsters. Among the Kalinago people of Dominica, ancient oral tales speak of Bakwa, a colossal, diamond-crested spirit serpent large enough to scale mountain cliffs and reshape volcanic terrain.
Bakwa is the trusty sidekick of Maboyo, a fearsome serpentine entity governing tropical storms, violent chaos, and the unseen destructive forces of untamed island nature. Yet the most terrifying dragon-like creature in regional lore is unquestionably the Lusca, a ruthless abyssal cryptid lurking inside the deep underwater blue holes off Andros Island in the Bahamas.
Described by mariners as a multi-headed dragon or a monstrous 200-foot shark-octopus chimera with razor-sharp teeth, the Lusca generates violent whirlpools that drag entire fishing boats and helpless swimmers down into deep submarine caverns to devour them in the dark. However, since the invention of reason has pretty much put an end to scary folklore, mythical monsters have taken a habit of going undercover.
Photo: Apollo Automobil Now, a very different breed of ferocious predator has awakened, though this mechanical mythical creature actually nests in the engineering workshops of Gaimersheim, Germany. Christened the Apollo EVO Caribbean Dragon, the carbon-fiber beast built by Germany’s only dedicated hypercar manufacturer, Apollo Automobil GmbH, has just crossed the Atlantic Ocean to North America to see what local exotic rivals and track lap records it can feast on.
Its official North American hunting ground will be the 2026 Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, where the radical new Apollo EVO is scheduled to stage its continental public debut. Running for four days from October 29 to November 1, the prestigious Nevada gathering will host this first customer production example of the track-only machine alongside two of its most celebrated predecessors from the German boutique marque’s storied high-performance stable.
The exclusive Bavarian automaker is utilizing the Las Vegas showcase to celebrate 20 years of its proud Rebellious German Engineering. For the first time outside Europe, wealthy enthusiasts and collectors will witness a complete lineage display uniting the foundational Gumpert Apollo, the visceral Apollo Intensa Emozione, and the newly completed Apollo EVO on the same lawn, illustrating the technical evolution of a track-bred automotive design philosophy.
Photo: Apollo Automobil The appearance in the United States follows the dynamic global debut of the Apollo EVO at the 2026 Goodwood Festival of Speed in England earlier this summer. Chief Executive Officer Niko Konta emphasized that North America has long remained central to the global vision of Apollo Automobil GmbH, noting that the Concours at Wynn Las Vegas offers an ideal venue to introduce the hypercar to loyal clients and passionate fans.
Conceived as a direct, track-focused successor to the acclaimed Intensa Emozione (need I translate that from Italian? It’s Intense Emotion), the Apollo EVO represents a total rejection of modern automotive homogenization. Penned by chief designer Jowyn Wong, the coupe is strictly limited to a production run of 10 customer units alongside a solitary factory prototype.
Each example is priced from €3,000,000 before local taxes and delivery fees, positioning the vehicle among the most exclusive collector machines on the planet today. That’s 3,346,000 legal money of the United States. It’s a lot of money, with which a gearhead can buy a lot of automotive adrenaline from several other high-end houses of speed, with or without electric add-ons.
Photo: Apollo Automobil Every single customer commission acts as a bespoke engineering showcase, exemplified by the inaugural Caribbean Dragon specification arriving in Las Vegas. Its sculpted exterior comprises 75 individual carbon-fiber panels finished in a white-and-blue livery through an intricate eight-layer hand-painting process that alone demands roughly 1,000 hours of labor.
That’s on top of the 1,200 hours of meticulous assembly required by specialist master technicians to construct each complete rolling chassis from the ground up. Dragons are very demanding creatures, apparently, and very much contrary to popular belief.
At the heart of the Apollo EVO sits a screaming, naturally aspirated 6.3-liter V12 engine derived from Ferrari architecture and developed in partnership with Autotecnica Motori and HWA AG. Displacing 6,262 cc and eschewing both turbochargers and hybrid electrification, the 12-cylinder powerplant revs all the way to 9,000 rpm, generating 800 hp and 765 Nm of torque (564 lb-ft) at 6,750 rpm to deliver an authentic motorsport soundtrack and immediate throttle response.
Photo: Apollo Automobil Instead of adopting a conventional dual-clutch transmission, engineers mated the high-revving engine to a racing-derived 6-speed Hewland sequential gearbox operated via an electro-pneumatic paddle-shift system. Because the entire vehicle tips the scales at just 1,300 kg, that ferocious rear-wheel-drive output propels the coupe from 0 to 62 mph in a blistering 2.7 seconds, while copious grip and stability allow the machine to reach a top speed of 208 mph (335 kph).
The visual drama on the Apollo EVO is matched by its functional aerodynamic violence, spearheaded by longitudinal aero fins and an electronically adjustable active rear spoiler. At 186 mph, the aero package generates a staggering 1,350 kg of downforce, exceeding the dry weight of the car itself.
In other words: if someone has the audacity, money, drive, and will to build a life-sized Hot Wheels track with a long-enough upside-down straight, the Apollo EVO Caribbean Dragon will casually do a flat-out inverted overhead pass. At 300 kph. I’d actually buy front-row tickets to see it happen.
Rearward airflow exits around an optional 3D-printed titanium Dragon Skin exhaust system, which naturally develops vivid blue heat patina as exhaust temperatures climb on track.
Photo: Apollo Automobil Underneath its aggressive skin, the hypercar utilizes an ultra-rigid carbon-fiber monocoque tub weighing only 105 kg, paired with carbon-ceramic disc brakes and forged center-lock wheels shod in Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 R tires.
Upward-swinging doors reveal a driver-centric, skeletonized interior architecture swathed in blue-tinted carbon fiber and white upholstery, complete with air conditioning, sensible track ergonomics, and 3 digital displays mounted directly above the bespoke racing steering wheel assembly.
This obsessive dedication to mechanical purity traces its roots back to 2004, when the company was originally established in Germany as Gumpert Sportwagenmanufaktur. The enterprise was the brainchild of Roland Gumpert, the former director of Audi Sport who had previously overseen a golden era of championship motorsport success.
Photo: Apollo Automobil Production of the brand’s inaugural model, the Gumpert Apollo, commenced in 2005, merging lightweight race engineering with strictly functional aerodynamic body design.
International stardom arrived in 2008 when a Gumpert Apollo S shattered the famous Top Gear power lap record, leaving established exotic rivals trailing in its wake. Just one year later, in 2009, the German giant-killer secured an even more prestigious accolade at the Nürburgring Nordschleife, posting a 7:11.57 lap time that beat the previous production benchmark by almost 11 seconds and stood unchallenged by competitors for nearly two full years.
Although Roland Gumpert eventually passed the torch to a new leadership team that rebranded the company as Apollo Automobil in honor of his original creation, those foundational principles remain intact. That unbroken bloodline, stretching from the 2005 Gumpert Apollo through the radical 2017 Apollo Intensa Emozione to the new 800 hp Apollo EVO Caribbean Dragon, will now take center stage for North American audiences at Wynn Las Vegas this week.

Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported a 16% increase in third-quarter core adjusted earnings per share Wednesday, as higher freight volumes and growth in grain and intermodal revenue helped offset rising fuel costs.
Revenue rose to C$4.22 billion ($3.01 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from $2.61 billion a year earlier , the Calgary-based company (NYSE: CP ) said in earnings released after the close of markets. Core adjusted diluted earnings increased to 91 cents per share from 78 cents, while reported diluted earnings rose 3% to 74 cents from 72 cents. Freight volumes, measured in revenue ton-miles, increased 6%.
“CPKC delivered solid results, powered by momentum across our unrivaled North American network, countering macroeconomic headwinds during the quarter,” President and Chief Executive Keith Creel said in the release. “The railroad is running very well, our service remains strong, and we continue to deliver growth across key markets, including grain, intermodal and merchandise.”
Grain revenue climbed to $644 million from $500 million in the third quarter of 2025, while intermodal revenue increased to $581 million from $476 million. Revenue from energy, chemicals and plastics rose to $544 million from $499 million, and automotive revenue reached $266 million, up from $244 million. Coal revenue was nearly unchanged at $181 million.
The gains lifted operating income to $1.06 billion from $955 million, although expenses increased faster than revenue. Fuel expense rose to $475 million from $296 million, while compensation and benefits increased to $507 million from $441 million.
CPKC’s operating ratio —operating expenses as a percentage of revenue and a key efficiency indicator— worsened to 64.8% from 63.5%. Its core adjusted operating ratio increased to 61.9% from 60.7%. The company said higher fuel prices added 1.7 percentage points to the reported ratio and 1.9 percentage points to the core adjusted figure.
Despite higher operating income, net income attributable to controlling shareholders edged down to $653 million from $655 million. Reported earnings per share nevertheless increased as the weighted-average diluted share count fell to 877.6 million from 911.4 million.
Income tax expense increased to $319 million from $211 million. The quarter included a $67 million tax charge related to Canadian tax reassessments associated with the Kansas City Southern acquisition in 2023, along with a $12 million expense from a Mexican tax settlement.
The company also disclosed $12 million in advisory costs related to its analysis and advocacy concerning the U.S. Surface Transportation Board ’s review of the proposed Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP )–Norfolk Southern (NYSE: N SC ) merger.
Cash generated by operating activities increased to $1.10 billion from $905 million a year earlier. Spending on additions to properties declined to $437 million from $613 million, while cash used to purchase common shares totaled $1.02 billion.
Creel said disciplined execution and a “robust commercial pipeline” supported the company’s confidence in meeting its annual commitments.

Dusty 1971 Nova Has the Ideal Combo: One Owner, Low Survivor Miles, Great Condition, Needs One Thing
10 photos
Photo: eBay.com/netr2
Chevrolet didn’t go well into the seventies. In fact, all of GM had it rough for the debut of that emotional roller-coaster decade. Strikes (the biggest in US automotive history), the oil embargo, the EPA, the imports – all coaxed fortunes to bring the hammer down hard on the corporation. Even so, the Bowtie still manage to deliver, and this 1971 Nova survivor is the perfect example of that resilience.
Tucked tightly against a graffiti-sprayed cinder-block wall where the word “NOVA” shares space with the names “Toni,” “Chuck,” and “Sarah,” a 1971 Chevrolet Nova coupe has emerged from decades of peaceful slumber. This original-owner garage find shows 40,489 miles (65,161 kilometers) on its odometer and remains in running, unmolested condition, wearing a thick blanket of dry storage dust rather than the damp rot that ruins many forgotten classics across America.
Finished in factory dark green, the exterior sheet metal is straight and complete, showing only honest surface oxidation across the hood and roof where the original paint has thinned over the past 55 years. All factory brightwork remains in place, including the chrome front bumper, window moldings, round driver-side mirror, amber side markers, and front fender scripts, while the car sits on deflated tires mounted on plain 14-inch steel wheels.
Inside the cabin, the seller's claim that the car is dusty rather than moldy rings true when inspecting the olive-green upholstery and trim. The perforated vinyl headliner is taut with intact factory stitching, flanking the original dome lamp and shoulder-belt clips, while the driver-side door panel retains its manual crank and armrest. A vertical split marks the green dash pad above the horizontal-sweep 120 mph instrument cluster speedometer.
Photo: eBay.com/netr2 Popping open the trunk reveals solid floor pans still coated in factory black-and-aqua spatter paint, housing a vintage spare wheel and tire secured by its wing-nut clamp alongside a plastic bag of original literature. Under the hood, the untouched engine bay cradles the factory inline-six powerplant beneath its single-snorkel air cleaner, accompanied by a manual drum-brake master cylinder on the firewall that confirms unassisted four-wheel drum brakes and manual steering.
Chevrolet introduced the Chevy II for the 1962 model year after developing the conventional compact in just 18 months to counter the runaway success of the Ford Falcon. Initially, Nova served as the top trim level of the Chevy II before becoming the model's sole nameplate in 1969. The iconic moniker spanned five separate generations across 22 production years, running from 1962 through 1979 and returning from 1985 through 1988.
Those five iterations comprised the first generation from 1962 to 1965, the squared-off second generation from 1966 to 1967, the semi-fastback third generation from 1968 to 1974 (from which this car stemmed), the European-styled fourth generation from 1975 to 1979, and the front-wheel-drive fifth generation built jointly with Toyota from 1985 to 1988.
Photo: eBay.com/netr2 Among enthusiasts and sales ledgers alike, the third generation reigns as the best all-time generation, blending muscular proportions with massive commercial appeal.
Across its initial 18-year rear-wheel-drive run from 1962 to 1979, Chevrolet manufactured 4,698,781 units of the Chevy II and Nova. The best all-time year of production arrived in 1974, when oil-crisis demand for compact cars pushed factory output to a record 390,537 units. That peak surpassed the 372,626 cars built in 1963 and the 369,509 cars assembled in 1973, although 1973 set the all-time Super Sport record with 35,542 examples.
For the 1971 model year, a 67-day United Auto Workers strike in late 1970 curtailed assembly schedules, dropping total Nova production to 194,878 cars across the two body styles. Buyers ordered 143,235 units of the two-door coupe and 51,643 units of the four-door sedan. Base prices started at $2,175 at launch and rose to $2,376 for the 6-cylinder two-door coupe like this car, while V8 coupes carried a $2,471 base sticker.
Photo: eBay.com/netr2 Chevrolet streamlined the 1971 engine roster by retiring the 153-cubic-inch (2.5-liter) four-cylinder, 230-cubic-inch (3.8-liter) inline-six, and big-block V8s. Of the 194,878 US-built cars, 94,928 carried the 250-cube inline-six (65,891 coupes and 29,037 sedans), while 99,950 featured V8 power, split between 77,344 coupes and 22,606 sedans.
Including Canadian Acadians, transmission installations totaled 126,921 Powerglide 2-speed automatics, 71,810 Turbo Hydra-Matic 350 3-speed automatics, 31,626 column 3-speed manuals, 3,950 Muncie 4-speeds, and 2,993 Torque-Drive semi-automatics.
The green coupe in this story belongs to the 65,891-unit cohort of six-cylinder two-door coupes and retains its RPO L22 250-cubic-inch (4.1-liter) Turbo-Thrift Six. Equipped with a seven-main-bearing cast-iron block, an 8.5:1 compression ratio, and a single-barrel Rochester carburetor, this powerplant delivered 145 hp (147 PS) gross or 110 hp (112 PS) net at 4,200 rpm and 235 lb-ft (319 Nm) of torque at 1,600 rpm to its 2-speed Powerglide.
Photo: eBay.com/netr2 Buyers wanting V8 muscle in 1971 had a trio of small-block choices with 8.5:1 compression. The L14 307-cubic-inch (5.0-liter) 2-barrel V8 generated 200 hp (203 PS) and 300 lb-ft (407 Nm), while the L65 350-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) 2-barrel V8 produced 245 hp (248 PS) and 350 lb-ft (475 Nm). The best engine offered in 1971 was the L48 350-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) 4-barrel V8, delivering 270 hp (274 PS) and 360 lb-ft (488 Nm) gross.
Special factory variants for 1971 included 7,015 examples of the RPO Z26 Nova SS—which mandated the 270 hp (274 PS) L48 350 V8—and 7,700 examples of the striped RPO YF1 Rally Nova. Earlier third-generation models also spawned iconic dealer-built titans, led by Don Yenko of Canonsburg, Pennsylvania. After building 37 big-block 427-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) 450 hp (456 PS) Yenko Super Novas in 1969, Yenko commissioned 175 COPO 9010 Yenko Deuce Novas.
Those 1970 Yenko Deuce coupes packed the solid-lifter 350-cubic-inch (5.7-liter) LT-1 V8 rated at 360 hp (365 PS) and 380 lb-ft (515 Nm), while high-performance dealerships such as Baldwin-Motion, Nickey Chevrolet, Fred Gibb, and Dick Harrell shoehorned 427-cubic-inch (7.0-liter) and 454-cubic-inch (7.4-liter) big-block V8s into third-generation bodies.
Photo: eBay.com/netr2 Because so many humble six-cylinder coupes were later gutted to build big-block clones, finding an uncut, original-paint 1971 survivor has become somewhat of a treat nowadays. Particularly when said find is still titled in the original buyer’s name, has under 50k miles on it, and looks like it teleported itself to 2026, instead of sitting through the decades hidden in a garage/graffiti studio.
Whether kept as the patinated six-cylinder cruiser or used as a rust-free canvas, this 40,489-mile (65,161-kilometer) 1971 Chevrolet Nova is currently offered for sale on eBay at $8,000 - or best offer. The coupe is sold as-is with a clean original title, and the buyer must pay for and arrange transportation. The seller plans to inflate the tires and roll it outside for full undercarriage photos – unless some quick-draw car nut snatches it first.

Don’t want to pay full price? Used EVs with low miles, like the Hyundai IONIQ 5 and Ford Mustang Mach-E, are selling on the secondhand market for $25,000 or less.
Top-selling used EVs you can find for under $25,000
With a flood of electric cars returning from lease this year and soaring gas prices, used EVs are suddenly flying off the lot.
Used EV sales rose to a record 3.3% of total used vehicle sales last month, up from 2.9% in August, according to Cox Automotive .
Used ICE vehicle sales, on the other hand, dropped 4.4% in September as buyers flocked to more efficient options.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
As expected, Tesla remains the leading used EV brand, followed by Ford, Chevrolet, Hyundai, and BMW.
By model, the Nissan Ariya led growth, with sales up 42.5% in September, followed by the Chevy Equinox EV (+41.9%), Kia EV9 (+36.2%), and Chevy Blazer EV (+30.2%), while the Ford Mustang Mach-E (+14.7%) and Tesla Model Y (+13.8 %) also saw more demand.
With more options to choose from, which one is best for you? To help you decide, Edmunds , which has tested nearly all of them, put together a list of four top used electric SUVs available for under $25,000.
Chevy Equinox EV (Source: Chevrolet)
Chevy Equinox EV
The first one on the list was the Chevy Equinox EV , or as GM used to call it, “America’s most affordable 315+ range” electric vehicle.
After it arrived in 2024, the Chevy Equinox EV quickly became one of the top-selling electric vehicles in the US outside Tesla, winning over buyers with enough space for a family and plenty of driving range at an affordable price.
Chevy Equinox EV interior (Source: GM)
The Chevy Equinox EV offers up to 319 miles of EPA-estimated driving range. It’s a great fit for those looking for a smaller, more efficient SUV that still offers plenty of interior space.
Edmunds says it’s worth upgrading to the 2LT trim, which adds heated front seats and a heated steering wheel, a wireless phone charger, adaptive cruise control, and a 360-degree HD Surround Vision camera system.
2023 Ford Mustang Mach-E (Source: Ford)
Ford Mustang Mach-E
Next on the list was the Ford Mustang Mach-E , which has also remained a top seller since it went on sale in 2021.
Ford tapped into its iconic Mustang nameplate to help attract new buyers. The Mustang Mach-E came well equipped with a large 15.5″ infotainment screen with Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto and Ford Co-Pilot360 Assist+.
2023 Ford Mustang Mach-E interior (Source: Ford)
While the GT is the most fun to drive, Edmunds said the Premium trim may be your best bet. It still offers plenty of performance while adding standard features like heated front seats and a heated steering wheel.
It’s also worth upgrading to the extended-range battery pack, which offers up to 320 miles of range on the Premium RWD model. You should be able to find used 2021 to 2023 Mach-E’s for under $25,000.
2024 Hyundai IONIQ 5 (Source: Hyundai)
Hyundai IONIQ 5
Another top-selling electric SUV, the Hyundai IONIQ 5 continues to win over buyers with its bold design, long-range capabilities, fast charging, and a surprisingly spacious interior.
2024 Hyundai IONIQ 5 interior (Source: Hyundai)
Edmunds says plenty of used 2022 to 2024 IONIQ 5s with low mileage are available for under $25,000.
While the base SE Standard Range is the cheapest, it only offers an EPA range of 220 miles. Upgrading to the Extended Range battery, which is used on all other trims, provides up to 303 miles of range.
2023 Volkswagen ID.4 AWD Pro S (Source: Volkswagen US Media Site)
Volkswagen ID.4
The Volkswagen ID.4 went on sale in the US in 2021 as one of the earlier mainstream electric SUVs.
It was updated in 2024, but up until the 2023 model year, the VW ID.4 offered an EPA range of up to 275 miles, depending on the configuration.
2023 Volkswagen ID.4 AWD Pro S interior (Source: Volkswagen US Media Site)
Finding a low-mileage used 2023 ID.4 shouldn’t be hard, but upgrading to the Pro S trim might be worth it.
Volkswagen updated the 2023 ID.4 with a new 12″ infotainment display and Park Assist Plus. The Pro S trim gained a fixed panoramic roof, V-Tex synthetic leather seating, and a heated steering wheel.

Analysts hailed the Phase 3 head and neck cancer results as a big victory for an asset central to Genmab’s growth plans.
A late-stage trial of Genmab’s petosemtamab hit its co-primary endpoints at the first interim analysis, the biotech said Wednesday, completing a clean sweep of victories in a high-stakes run of readouts.
The LiGeR-HN1 study tested petosemtamab, a bispecific antibody targeting EGFR and LGR5, in combination with Merck’s Keytruda in nearly 700 patients with PD-L1-positive head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Given as a first-line treatment, the combination significantly improved overall survival (OS) and objective response rate (ORR) compared to single-agent Keytruda, meeting its co-primary endpoints.
The investigational combination reduced the risk of death by 50%, regardless of HPV status.
William Blair analysts in a Wednesday morning note called the result “exceedingly positive,” while their counterparts at Truist Securities hailed the OS finding as “highly compelling and potentially practice-changing.”
Genmab has now delivered positive data on three key candidates in quick succession. At the start of October, the biotech was preparing to share Phase 3 data on its AbbVie-partnered bispecific antibody Epkinly, the antibody-drug conjugate rinatabart sesutecan (Rina-S) and petosemtamab. Weeks later, Genmab has positive data from all three studies.
Genmab’s stock rose 29% to $57.57 in early trading on Wednesday.
Pipeline
Epkinly data only one of Genmab’s make-or-break readouts ahead of steep sales erosion
Bracing for patent losses on its cornerstone product Darzalex, Genmab has bet its future on three cancer programs that will deliver pivotal readouts in quick succession.
October 20, 2026
·
5 min read
·
Nick Paul Taylor
Read more
“We view the Rina-S and peto OS wins as particularly striking and believe all three franchises can support multibillion-dollar opportunities,” Truist analysts said. “Full data remain important given the first interim analysis, and we look for additional color on OS maturity, absolute ORR, safety and regulatory timing.”
Genmab has yet to disclose the median OS or ORR. Based on Keytruda’s historical performance in the setting, Truist analysts estimate that the petosemtamab combination may have achieved a median OS of about 30 months, broadly in line with the 28.2-month result seen in Phase 2. The analysts forecast that the ORR result could be in the 44% to 58% range.
The earlier-than-expected interim OS hit could accelerate Genmab’s path to market, Truist said. Analysts had initially expected OS results in 2027.
The OS success suggests “a particularly strong treatment effect” and supports potential approval in 2027, Truist said—ahead of the 2028 approval currently modeled by Truist. Bringing petosemtamab to market earlier than expected would give Genmab more time to grow sales of the product before the expiration of patents on Darzalex, its Johnson and Johnson-partnered multiple myeloma drug.
Preparing for the patent loss, Genmab invested in Epkinly, an internally discovered program, and struck deals for petosemtamab and Rina-S. Petosemtamab represented the biggest bet, with Genmab acquiring the drug candidate in its $8 billion takeover of Merus in September 2025.
Mergers & acquisitions
Genmab Buys Rising Cancer Star Merus for $8B
The centerpiece of the acquisition is petosemtamab, Merus’ bispecific antibody targeting EGFR and LGR5, which in May demonstrated best-in-class potential for head-and-neck cancer.
September 29, 2025
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
Bicara Therapeutics’ ficerafusp alfa is a potential competitor to petosemtamab, with the biotech on track to report interim Phase 3 HNSCC data in mid-2027. Shares in Bicara, which is only enrolling HPV-negative patients in its HNSCC trial, were down 48% to $8.94 as of publication.
BMO Capital Markets took a more positive stance on Bicara, however, saying in a Wednesday morning note that “on first blush,” the stock weakness doesn’t match the outlook for the company. The early OS result for Genmab “increases our confidence in ficerafusp delivering OS success at its mid-2027 Ph3 interim,” the analysts said.

Owner Takes His Ford Mustang Dark Horse to a Tuner, Goes Home With GTD Power
17 photos
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube
Why pay over $350,000 for the Ford Mustang GTD when a tuner can give you GTD power on a Mustang Dark Horse for a fraction of the price? This is what the owner of this muscle car must have thought the moment he drove to a tuner in Houston, Texas. A couple of weeks later, he went home with 800 horsepower. Nope! No turbos involved in this build!
Some car guys don't do stock. Factory specification just doesn't cut it for them. Take the owner of this 2026 Ford Mustang Dark Horse . A short while ago, he drove home in his brand-new Mustang Dark Horse, powered by the 5.0-liter Coyote V8 with naturally aspirated firepower.
The V8 pumped out 500 horsepower (507 metric horsepower) and 418 pound-feet (567 Newton meters) of torque for a run from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.1 seconds and a top speed of 166 mph (267 kph) when equipped with the ten-speed automatic transmission, like this car is.
The owner wanted to take the Mustang Dark Horse to the next level. So now, he can beat the hell out of his brand-new toy, with no compromise on reliability and driveability. It is still a perfect daily driver, without turning violent.
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube An aftermarket Magnuson TVS2650 supercharger, the same one that the tuners use on many General Motors' cars like the Chevrolet Corvettes and Camaros, added over 250 rear-wheel horsepower. But how did they get that far?
They came up with an extra expansion tank to keep things cool under the hood. An extra intercooler pump made its way into the engine bay, along with a new heat exchanger. The factory air box remained, and so did the headers, exhaust, and fuel system. The car still drives on pump gas and comes with a factory-style warranty offered by the tuner.
The Mustang Dark Horse drove into the shop making 421 rear-wheel horsepower and 353 pound-feet of rear-wheel torque and drove out making 676.7 rear-wheel horsepower and 537.8 pound-feet of rear-wheel torque. That’s a solid 256 rear-wheel horsepower and 185 pound-feet of rear-wheel torque.
That would be roughly 800 horsepower and 635 pound-feet at the crank. In the meantime, the most powerful road-going Mustang, the GTD, comes with 815 horsepower (826 metric horsepower) and 664 pound-feet (900 Newton meters) of torque for a run from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 2.7 seconds and a top speed of 202 mph (325 kph).
Photo: Late Model Racecraft | YouTube The tuner can squeeze more out of the 5.0-liter V8 in case the owner comes back for more. So why buy a Mustang GTD when a dialed-up Dark Horse can do nearly just as good?
Now, Steven Fereday of Late Model Racecraft took the Mustang Dark Horse out for a spin to make sure that it runs, drives, shifts, and behaves properly with the massive power gain that it will go home with.
The car blows the tires off in first gear with traction control off and grabs the second gear to regain grip and takes off the line like there is no tomorrow, gluing the driver into the seat, delivering torque right from the get-go.
The Ford Mustang Dark Horse starts at $70,570, while the Mustang GTD is a $350,000 deal before adding fees and options. Late Model Racecraft does not disclose the price of the upgrade, but it is surely far under the price of the GTD, even though it brings nearly as much power.

How Much Is a Used Ferrari 458 Spider Worth Today in USA?
12 photos
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago
Even though it’s been dead for many years, the Ferrari 458 continues to gain traction in our news feed, and if you wonder why, then you may want to throw away that petrolhead license, because you clearly do not need it.
Not only has this model aged like fine wine, but it is also the Prancing Horse’s last rear mid-engined, rear-wheel drive supercar to feature a naturally aspirated mill. Its successor, the 488, which was made between 2015 and 2020, is twin-turbocharged, and so is the F8 that followed from 2019 to 2023, whereas the modern-day 296 is not only turbocharged, but also partially electrified.
Ferrari made the 458 between 2009 and 2015 at its Maranello factory (where else?) in Italy. The F430’s successor is 178.2 inches (4,527 mm) long, 76.3 inches (1,937 mm) wide, and 47.8 inches (1,213 mm) tall. It has a wheelbase length of 104.3 inches (2,650 mm), a curb weight of a little over 1.5 metric tons (3,450 pounds), and was offered in two body styles: a two-door berlinetta (coupe) and a two-door convertible.
The lineup comprised the 458 Italia (Coupe), 458 Spider (Convertible), the 458 Speciale and Speciale A (Aperta / convertible), the 458 Italia China Edition, and the 458 MM Speciale, Pininfarina Sergio, and SP13 EC one-offs, which used the same underpinnings as the mainstream 458.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago With this short history lesson behind us, it is time to put the spotlight on the Ferrari 458 Spider pictured above. It is a 2013 model year car, according to the vendor, and it features a glossy black look on the outside. It rides on black five-spoke alloys, has red brake calipers for a bit of contrast, and is decorated with the Prancing Horse logos all around.
Step inside, and you will see a mix of black leather and black Alcantara upholstery, wrapped around most touchable surfaces. There is also some carbon fiber trim, and we can see that this machine has red stitching for contrast, including on the seats, dashboard panel, door cards, and center console, black Prancing Horse emblems embroidered into the headrests, and a very simple and very cool overall layout compared to more modern supercars, this writer thinks.
There is only a tiny bit of wear on the driver’s seat outer bolster, so this particular Ferrari 458 Spider looks almost as good today as it did back when it originally left the dealership more than a decade ago. The vendor did not say much about it, so we do not know whether it has paint protection film on the outside, but the exterior also looks extremely fine, at least in the pictures that accompany the ad.
We do not know how many owners this machine has had over the years, no details surrounding the title have been released at the time of writing, and we also have no idea when it was last serviced. What we can tell you, though, is that the odometer read around 18,000 miles (29,000 km) at the time of cataloging.
Photo: Instagram | motorcarsofchicago Power is supplied by a 4.5-liter naturally aspirated V8 engine, which was good for 562 horsepower (570 ps/419 kW ) at 9,000 rpm and 398 pound-feet (540 Nm) of torque at 6,000 rpm back when the supercar was still new. The Ferrari 458 Italia , namely the fixed-roof model, took 3.4 seconds to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, which made it some two-tenths of a second faster than the iconic Ferrari Enzo.
But what about the Ferrari 458 Spider, you ask? Well, with no outside intervention, it completed the sprint just as fast as the coupe, though its top speed was a tiny bit lower at 199 mph (320 kph), as opposed to the 458 Italia’s 202 mph (325 kph).
Depending on the mileage, options, and overall condition, a Ferrari 458 typically retails between $165,000 and over $450,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America. The 458 Spider is a few tens of thousands more expensive than the 458 Italia, and models such as the 458 Speciale and 458 Speciale A can easily venture into the seven-digit realm.
Thus, your pockets must be quite deep if you dream about owning a 458, but does this also apply to the pictured example? In short, yes! That’s because this Italian supercar is on the very pricey side of things. We found it advertised on social media by @motorcarsofchicago, with an asking price of $379,995 attached to it at the time of writing.
The vendor says it accepts trade-ins, offers financing, and is not particularly fond of DMs. Therefore, you know what to do if you want to sign your name on the dotted line of this 2013 Ferrari 458 Spider , don’t you? But is this supercar worth the asking price, or do you feel like it is a bit too much? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Motor Cars of Chicago (@motorcarsofchicago)

Lamborghini Miura Turns 60, No Better Way To Celebrate Than This $9,900 Limited Edition Pen
19 photos
Photo: Montegrappa
The pen is mightier than the sword. But is it mightier than the original Supercar, the Lamborghini Miura, in building an owner the aura of refinement, superiority, elegance, luxury, and class? Montegrappa thinks it is.
A pen is a very discreet personal item - more elusive than a wristwatch, less conspicuous than cufflinks, and less used than a necktie stickpin. And yet, it holds more power than any other item in the world. It makes words into law, it shapes destinies more than all of humanity's arsenals, and it has power over time itself - it writes both history and the future. And it does all that with something as simple as a signature.
But simple it is not, as Giuseppe Aquila, owner and CEO of Montegrappa, gracefully explained for us in an interview. So, what's the story about the Miura? Glad you asked. Read on and learn how a writing instruments company put pen to paper (literally and metaphorically), and crafted one of the most beautiful homages to one of the most beautiful and emblematic (Lamborghini) cars ever made.
When the Lamborghini Miura debuted at the Geneva Motor Show in March 1966, its racing-derived transverse mid-engine layout did not just revolutionize motoring, it single-handedly invented the supercar. Now celebrating its 60th anniversary in October 2026, the Sant'Agata Bolognese icon is being immortalized by Montegrappa. "We're very proud of this collaboration because personally Miura for me is one of the best cars ever produced," Aquila told Autoevolution during our conversation.
Photo: Montegrappa Why pair a legendary Italian supercar with a traditional ink instrument in our heavily digitized modern era? Because a bespoke pen commands a presence that rivals any exotic machine parked outside. "In our case, first of all, our pens are not just simply writing instruments," Aquila explained. "They are a status symbol, they are accessories, like a fashion accessory, and the fountain pen is also an item linked to culture".
While smartphones handle daily notes, luxury pens seal life's biggest milestones. "You use the pen to sign an important contract, you use a pen to sign when you're getting married, maybe when you're getting divorced, you use it when you buy a house," Aquila noted. Furthermore, a Montegrappa study conducted with a neuroscientist proved handwriting engages the amygdala and long-term memory, helping students perform two times better than digital typists.
That tangible connection between mechanics and emotion unites Bassano del Grappa with Sant'Agata Bolognese. "This is not our first collaboration with Lamborghini, so we are licensees of Lamborghini for writing instruments," Aquila said, recalling their first five-color series launched two years ago for the automaker's 60th anniversary.
Photo: Montegrappa In October 2026, Montegrappa releases two new collections before Christmas, namely the accessible open-edition Lamborghini Icon and the flagship Automobili Lamborghini Miura.
To craft the Automobili Lamborghini Miura pen, Montegrappa's designers closely studied the original Bertone-styled supercar. "We only make 60 pieces of each version, so it means 60 pieces yellow, 60 pieces green, 60 pieces black, of either the fountain pen version and the rollerball version," Aquila explained. Selected by Automobili Lamborghini from 1966 best-sellers, the 3 shades, Giallo Fly, Verde Miura, and Black, apply genuine car paint onto aluminum barrels.
Every millimeter of the silhouette reinterprets the Miura's unmistakable proportions, crowned by a miniature pop-up headlamp on the cap. "This headlamp, you could actually tilt it forward, you can open and move forward, right? So even the pen has a similar mechanism," Aquila beamed. "There's a special mechanism, a push-pull: you push and it comes out, and then you can press it in and it will click back into position".
Photo: Montegrappa "The headlamp itself is made of rock crystal, and the surface underneath the rock crystal is actually engraved with the same pattern, the same texture as the lamp itself," Aquila added. Other cues abound: the barrel end mirrors the rear Venetian louvres, the serial number sits on a honeycomb grille, the cap band echoes the side vents, the clip mimics the hood slats, and the wood-and-leather box replicates the seats.
Uncapping the fountain pen reveals an 18-karat gold nib electroplated in black ruthenium, stamped with the Automobili Lamborghini shield, offered in four iridium-tipped grades, and paired with Austrian ink and a CNC-turned vulcanized ebonite feeder. Unlike ABS plastic, ebonite retains memory. "Older cars like Miura, you needed some mileage to get the best, rodaggio we call it in Italian (editor’s note: break-in ), " Aquila compared, noting the feeder adapts to pressure over a period of two weeks.
Engineering this mechanical jewel stretched from early 2025 to October 2026. "Normally a project like this, from the idea to the actual introduction of the product into the market, requires from a minimum of one year to two years," the writing instruments supremo explained. Following one to two months of research and one month of Lamborghini design feedback, prototyping takes up to three months plus a couple more for final factory approval.
Photo: Montegrappa Once approved, Montegrappa builds a pre-series batch for brutal durability trials. "There is a drop test, so the pen is dropped from 120 cm on the floor and we see how it reacts," Aquila revealed. Beyond that 47.2-inch drop, pens are cycled in a climatic chamber from -4°F to 122°F (-20°C to +50°C) at 0% to 100% humidity, tested against human sweat, and tumbled with sharp metal keys.
Founded in 1912 as Elmo ahead of Tibaldi in 1916, Aurora in 1918, and Omas in 1921, Montegrappa operated uninterrupted through both World Wars and once employed 400 workers producing pens for Waterman and Sheaffer. After pioneering limited editions in 1992 and regaining family independence from Richemont, Aquila's 60 artisans cut annual output from 100,000 pens to below 50,000, including under 5,000 collector pieces that generate 50% of total sales.
Photo: Montegrappa Among those 60 specialists are hand-engravers, stone setters, and a trio of miniature painters, led by a master who, after having spent 26 years restoring Renaissance paintings in Valencia, Spain, needed six months to master curved barrels, and trained an apprentice for four years. Although fountain pens generate 60% of Montegrappa's revenue and rollerballs and ballpoints take 20% each, "with the Lamborghini pens, we sell more rollerballs than fountain pens, " Montegrappa’s boss observed.
Priced at 8,250 euros ($9,900) for the fountain pen and 6,850 euros ($8,250) for the rollerball, 30% to 40% of the entire Automobili Lamborghini Miura run is already pre-sold to loyal collectors reserving favorite numbers like 4, 8, 10, or 13. Backed by 35 years of stocked spare parts and custom-machined components that keep pens manufactured in 1912 writing today, a Miura pen crafted by Montegrappa "can be handed over from generation to generation," Aquila warmly concluded.

Caravancol's Classic Is a Proper Vintage-Inspired Travel Trailer That Fits As Many as Six People
6 photos
Photo: Caravancol
There are so many different brands in the world spitting out what they feel is the perfect vintage teardrop camper that we can easily get lost in all the details. However, every once in a while, a particular team comes along and shows us how it’s done. That crew is Caravancol, a Spain-born manufacturer banking on vintage design to grab everyone’s attention.
When I first saw the Classic from Caravancol, I couldn’t but help be reminded of American campers from back in the day, and I know that it’s the side panels at the kitchen that give us this impression . But what we’re working with here is actually a very modern camper, one built with timeless and trusted materials to give off that retro look.
Photo: Caravancol Materials like aluminum, wood, and composite insulation are called upon to give rise to the modern but retro Classic. It has an aluminum exterior that’s coated to keep the elements at bay, bamboo interior paneling, foam core insulation, and a plywood kitchen that looks downright flawless.
One neat trait is that the sides of the Classic are reinforced. We don’t know how, but they are, and it’s the main reason why we can see them carrying roof-top racks. So, these babies are clearly not so traditional in the sense that they do call upon modern building methods to give rise to it. Personally, I don’t know of a whole lot of traditional teardrop campers that can handle the added weight of a tent and occupants on its roof.
How much are we talking here? According to the spec sheet, up to 750 kg (1,653 lbs) is the max that a Classic can handle, and there’s a reason for that: it’s built over in Europe. Out there, you can operate an unbraked travel trailer as long as its GVWR remains at 750 kg or less and the combined weight of the trailer and vehicle doesn’t exceed 3,500 kg, without any special driver’s license classes.
Photo: Caravancol In its lightest configuration, the Classic also weighs a meaningless and very manageable weight of just 550 kg (1,213 lbs).
That however, sems to be the standard layout, with the manufacturer’s website showcasing additional upgrades, some of which do mess with the running gear and unlock brakes and axles with shock absorbers. Sounds like this one can handle some off-road use.
Speaking of upgrades, do note that the roof-rack is an optional feature here and will cost you a bit more to include in your build. If you do, however, it unlocks family use. Keep in mind that Caravancol mentions that sleeping capacity in their campers can be extended to as many as six.
While most of us are sure to think that this is made possible with an additional annex – it can – from what I could make out, the interior of a Classic can also include a bunk system for kids. If the tent is a three-person one, which the market does offer, then that’s that, six people. It’s not often that we can tap into this sort of ability with a teardrop camper.
Photo: Caravancol Before heading inside, allow me to point out that the exterior of this unit can also handle countless other pieces of gear, including a shower, solar panels, AC and heating units, and even a skylight. The latter does replace the AC, but falling asleep while staring at the stars is a must.
Oh, and let’s not forget the gorgeous and inspiring kitchen block, located at the rear of the camper, in traditional fashion. We have access to a cooker here, fridge, sink with water, ample cabinetry, and the electrical systems necessary to power said fridge and even coffee makers, kettles, all of that jazz.
Again, those side skirts also give this one its unique and vintage touch and is a feature that is used across the entire lineup from Caravancol. Couple that with the stained wood look, and you can see why I call this one vintage.
Photo: Caravancol The interior has that whole classic look and feel to it too, again, brought to life with the use of wood, in this case, mostly bamboo, and the cabinetry at the foot of the bed. Keep in mind that we can also call upon a TV and antenna and a modular mattress too, the latter being essential for adding a lounge experience inside.
A couple things to consider here are clearly price and the fact that this one is European, marking it as hand-off for anyone outside of that continent. You’ll have to handle shipping and DOT clearance if you do ship one outside of Europe.
As for the amount of cash that we need to drop on this one, Caravancol showcases a price tag of €16,800 ($18,800), and that seems to be without sales tax or VAT, as it’s called over in Europe. That said, there are some custom camper shops in the US that can spit out a camper like this one, so it may be best to act locally. Enjoy the trips out there.

Central Nevada Gold has outlined an initial gold resource at Mule Canyon in Nevada. Credit: Central Nevada Gold
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 28, 2026
Privately held Central Nevada Gold has outlined an initial gold resource at Mule Canyon in Nevada as it works towards a construction decision in 2028 on restarting the former open-pit operation.
The project near Battle Mountain hosts 11.9 million indicated tonnes grading 1.73 grams gold per tonne for 663,000 oz., according to an estimate effective July 1 and released Wednesday. A further 20.8 million inferred tonnes at 1.52 grams contain 1.02 million ounces.
“Our next priority is to demonstrate the technical and economic viability of recovering a substantial proportion of the resource over a long mine-life,” CEO Simon Griffiths said in a release.
The estimate gives the Toronto-based developer a basis for planning a return to production. The next steps include upgrading inferred material, which accounts for about 61% of the contained gold, establishing the economics and securing restart permits.
Restart studies
A prefeasibility study and permitting are underway, alongside infill drilling aimed at upgrading inferred resources to the indicated category. Central Nevada reported $18.5 million (C$26 million) in working capital.
SRK Consulting prepared the estimate using a cut-off grade of 0.5 gram gold per tonne.
The resources sit within conceptual pit shells based on a $3,800-per-oz. gold price and assumed metallurgical recovery of 93%.
Grade sensitivity
At a higher cut-off of 1.3 grams, the estimate includes 6.34 million indicated tonnes grading 2.46 grams for 502,000 oz. and 8.52 million inferred tonnes at 2.48 grams for 680,000 ounces.
That threshold retains about three-quarters of the indicated gold and two-thirds of the inferred gold reported at the base cut-off, while reducing the tonnage included. It is a sensitivity case, rather than a selected mine plan.
The company plans exploration and resource expansion drilling next year. Historical drill holes averaged 152 metres deep, and several areas remain open along strike and at depth, it said. Mineralized intercepts outside the conceptual pits provide targets for further work.
Restart funding
Central Nevada acquired Mule Canyon from Newmont (NYSE, ASX: NEM) earlier this year. The company reports about 500,000 oz. of historical production and says the site has grid power, water rights and an active federal plan of operations.
A February fact sheet from Nevada’s Division of Environmental Protection described Mule Canyon as permanently closed and said proposed on-site processing facilities had never been built and were no longer authorized under its state water pollution control permit. That permit is separate from the federal plan of operations cited by Central Nevada. The fact sheet predates the acquisition and does not establish the project’s current restart approval status. The company says it is advancing permits for a potential restart.
On Sept. 1, Central Nevada completed a $33-million financing led by a fund managed by Orion Mine Finance Management. The company said it expected the proceeds to fully fund drilling, the prefeasibility study and permitting.
Orion invested $25 million through equity and a prepaid gold and silver stream, with strategic shareholders providing the remaining $8 million through a private placement. The stream entitles Orion to 1.5% of Mule Canyon’s gold production and 4.8% of its silver output, subject to adjustments under the agreement.
Central Nevada said in September it was also evaluating a listing on a North American stock exchange as it pursued a strategy of building a multi-asset precious metals producer in Nevada.

El Teniente mine smelter. ( Image courtesy of: Codelco | Flickr. )
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 28, 2026
Copper prices are set to stay near record highs next year as new mines struggle to keep pace with demand from power grids and data centres, the World Bank forecasts.
The bank raised its 2027 copper price estimate 18% from April to $13,000 (C$18,250) per tonne, or about $5.90 per lb., in its October outlook , released Wednesday. That’s only 1.5% below the $13,200 average it now projects for this year.
“Commodity markets are being hit by several major shocks at once,” Ayhan Kose, the bank’s deputy chief economist, said in a news release . “Higher energy costs and trade disruptions are driving up prices across a broad range of commodities, threatening to worsen inflation, food insecurity and economic growth.”
For miners and investors, the outlook points to sustained demand for new copper supply alongside higher costs and an uneven recovery across other commodities. Electrification is supporting industrial metals, while weak construction weighs on iron ore and high silver prices encourage manufacturers to use less of it.
The bank expects its metals and minerals index, which includes base metals and iron ore but excludes precious metals, to rise 25% this year before easing 3.3% in 2027. Even after that decline, the index would stand 16% above its 2021 peak. The forecasts are calendar-year averages, based on information available through Oct. 14.
Supply limits
Long development timelines help explain why the bank expects prices to remain elevated. Investment is shifting toward industries that use more base metals, while exploration and mine construction can take more than a decade and refining capacity remains concentrated in a handful of countries.
Copper’s recent gains haven’t depended entirely on stronger consumption. Global demand slipped slightly in the first half, the bank found. Mine disruptions and the movement of refined metal into U.S. warehouses helped tighten availability elsewhere.
Uncertainty over possible U.S. import tariffs created a premium for copper traded on Comex over London Metal Exchange prices, drawing shipments toward the United States. That gap narrowed substantially by September, but uncertainty over tariffs taking effect in January could encourage further stockpiling and regional shortages.
Mine supply growth is expected to remain subdued as Indonesia deals with lingering weather-related disruptions and Chile faces operational constraints and declining grades. Demand should strengthen in 2027–28 through investment in electricity networks, data centres and electric vehicles.
Trade policy is adding another constraint. The Democratic Republic of Congo banned copper concentrate exports in August to encourage domestic processing, although exemptions could limit the immediate impact, the bank said. Its supporting data show 147 restrictive measures affecting critical minerals through September, against 63 measures easing trade. Those counts give every intervention equal weight, regardless of the volume of trade affected.
Uneven gains
The bank’s upward revisions extend beyond copper. It increased next year’s tin forecast 22% from April to $45,000 a tonne and its zinc estimate 13% to $3,100. Both metals are still expected to fall about 11%-12% from this year’s averages as supply improves.
Iron ore faces a different market. Weak Chinese construction and rising supply from established exporters and Guinea’s Simandou project are expected to keep pressure on prices. The bank retained its April forecast of $95 a dry tonne for 2027, down from $98 this year.
Nor does expanding clean-energy demand lift every battery material equally. Cobalt and lithium prices fell 25% and 13%, respectively, in the third quarter. Restarted Australian mines, resumed Zimbabwean concentrate exports and softer Chinese electric-vehicle sales momentum weighed on lithium.
Nickel faces competition from nickel-free lithium-iron-phosphate batteries. Stainless steel, which accounts for about two-thirds of nickel use, remains its main demand driver. The bank expects nickel prices to be little changed next year.
Precious pullback
Gold is forecast to average $4,250 per oz. in 2027, down 7.6% from this year’s projected $4,600. The bank trimmed next year’s estimate from $4,300 in April, expecting investment demand and central-bank buying to moderate while remaining supportive.
Those two sources accounted for about half of gold demand in the first half. Jewellery consumption has declined sharply since 2023, while high prices are encouraging recycling. Mine production is expected to increase only modestly.
Silver’s industrial exposure creates a sharper trade-off. The bank projects an average of $62 per oz. next year, down 11% from $70 this year and below April’s $65 forecast.
High prices are encouraging solar manufacturers to reduce silver use and substitute copper in the electrical contacts of photovoltaic cells. Growing consumption from electronics, data centres, vehicles and power infrastructure should partly offset those losses, but recycling and modest mine-supply gains are expected to ease market tightness.
Shared shocks
A companion study offers another caution for commodity investors: price volatility becomes more connected during periods of global stress.
Using daily data for 15 commodities from 2006 through June 2026, the bank found roughly one-third of volatility was associated with shocks in other commodity markets. About half of those connections occurred within broad commodity groups.
Industrial metals and food were the main net transmitters of volatility. Copper and silver stood out as bridges between markets, alongside oil and maize. These are statistical relationships; the model doesn’t establish that a shock in one market causes volatility in another.
Energy exposure
For producers, higher metal prices can come with more expensive fuel, power and processing inputs. The bank expects European electricity costs to continue constraining aluminum and zinc smelting, while disruption to Middle Eastern sulphur shipments could raise nickel-processing costs in Indonesia.
U.S. diesel prices reached record levels in October, the bank found. Damage to refineries in the Gulf region and Russia could keep diesel supplies tight even as crude exports recover, the bank said.
Its baseline assumes Brent crude eases to $79 a barrel next year from $91 in 2026. Even that lower forecast is 13% above April’s $70 estimate. An adverse scenario involving further energy-supply disruptions would put the 2027 average at $105.
Supply setbacks could therefore push metal prices above the forecasts while squeezing producers’ margins. If higher energy prices instead drive inflation, interest rates and financing costs high enough to weaken investment and manufacturing, the same shock could undermine industrial-metal demand.

This Sprinter Camper Van Breaks the Mold With a Rear Bathroom and a Manual Elevator Bed
15 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion
Today's featured build is based on a Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It was created earlier this year by the Auburn, California-based AdventureBumss. This company specializes in handcrafted homes on wheels that are designed to fit the needs of each customer.
This conversion was a partial build, in the sense that the customer provided the Sprinter which already had some work done, such as the floors and some cabinetry. Before we check out the inside, let me shortly mention some important exterior upgrades.
For starters, the Sprinter rides on alloy wheels wrapped in all-terrain tires. Next, at the front, you'll come across a massive Backwoods Adventure Mods bumper complete with an LED light bar and a winch. On the opposite end, there's a spare tire carrier attached to the driver-side door.
On top of the vehicle, the builders added a rack that holds a front-facing LED light bar and solar panels.
Other notable mods are side steps and power and water connections. The van came with two windows already installed, and AdventureBumss added three more windows: one on the side and two at the back.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion Stepping inside, you'll be greeted by a warm and roomy interior. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van and used after you set up camp.
Regarding aesthetics, the customer opted for a cohesive design with a slatted pine ceiling, wall panels and cabinetry with a raw wood look, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by white Corian solid surface countertops and brown leather drawer handles.
Above, you'll find the main sleeping arrangement. It's an elevator bed system that's much more primitive than the elevator beds we've seen in other camper vans.
Instead of having an electronically controlled system, this bed has two tow straps on each corner: one to lower and raise the bed and the other to stabilize it. They hook into factory D-rings or installed D-rings.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion Dead ahead of the entrance, you'll come across a simple seating area comprising a bench with a Lagun table. The bench is so long that it could double as a narrow bed.
Next, we have the kitchen, which is split into two units, one on each side of the living space. It features a fridge with a tiny freezer compartment and a copper sink with a pull-out tap and a filtered water faucet.
There's an abundant amount of counter space available - I can't imagine a meal so complicated that would require even more surface area.
Three overhead cabinets, several drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage in the kitchen. The latter houses a freshwater tank, an electric water heater, a pump, and a water filtration system.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion There's also a floor-to-ceiling unit on the driver side integrating a hanging closet and three drawers. Above it, the builders added a ceiling A/C unit.
Interestingly, the rear part of the interior is where you'll discover the bathroom and the garage. I said "interestingly" because few camper vans come with rear bathrooms.
The shower is integrated into a panel sitting on the side of the hallway - basically, you can wash yourself right in the middle of this part of the van and use a curtain to separate the area from the rest of the living space.
The water drains into a floor-integrated stainless steel pan, which then routes it to an under-mounted greywater tank. Moreover, a Maxxair vent fan above will draw out the moisture produced by showering.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion Opposite the shower, the builders fitted a small counter and two drawers. The larger drawer accommodates a portable toilet.
Finally, the garage sits on the driver's side, behind the panel holding the shower. It's accessible only from the back of the van, after opening the door on the left.
We don't know the specs of the power system inside this rig. However, based on other AdventureBumss creations, I'd assume that it's packing a 200 Ah lithium battery paired with a 3,000 W inverter.
The garage offers a decent amount of storage space. It has an open storage compartment that's about half of the interior height, as well as three drawers. You also get some charging points if you need to charge your gadgets.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / AdventureBumss Van Conversion The "command center" for the rig's utilities is integrated into the driver-side kitchen wall panel. It includes two standard outlets, a thermostat for the heater, two USB plugs, a battery monitor, an inverter controller, and a light switch.
All in all, this custom creation by Adventure Bumss packs all the essentials needed to hit the road in comfort. It's clear that a lot of work went into bringing the customer's vision to life, and I'm sure they were really happy with the result.
